clue.text: Possibly perceived perusing poetry, perhaps?

parts.note: the clue is itself a run of words all starting with P, so it shows the very device it describes

explanation.surface: Something you might notice while reading verse, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word of the clue begins with P, so the clue is an example of what it defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeating the same opening consonant across neighbouring words is the poetic device named here, as the four P-words show.

clue.text: Engages sailor on ship circumnavigating globe

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the sailor above the rest

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: circumnavigating says the ship letters go all the way round the globe

parts.note: SS is steamship
an orb is a globe

explanation.surface: A sailor signs up on a ship going round the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that absorbs you engages or engrosses your attention.

clue.text: Get Shakespearean role over McKellen finally

indicators.note: over, in a down clue, sets the role above the final letter

parts.note: King Lear is a Shakespeare title role

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the name McKellen

explanation.surface: Sir Ian McKellen finally lands a Shakespearean role.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian McKellen did indeed play King Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something, such as a fact or a point, is to learn or grasp it.

clue.text: So English following endless speculation about umpire

indicators.note: following puts English after the rest
about says the shortened speculation goes round the umpire
endless says the last letter comes off the speculation

parts.note: a theory is a speculation
ref, referee, is an umpire

explanation.surface: An English speculation about a match official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts THEORY to THEOR, which goes 'about' REF to make THEREFOR.
explanation.definitionFit: So and therefore are both connectives meaning as a consequence.

clue.text: Cross and coarse when overheard

indicators.note: when overheard says the word is heard, not seen, so take its sound

parts.note: coarse means rude

explanation.surface: Being angry and vulgar when someone listens in.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood is a crucifix, especially one above a church screen, so a cross.

clue.text: Censorious expression over banter with ace dropping class

parts.note: tut is the disapproving sound made by a censorious person
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

indicators.note: ace is A, and dropping says that letter falls lower in the word, one place down

parts.note: to rail is to jeer or jest at someone, here taken as banter

explanation.surface: A disapproving teacher tuts at chat while an ace pupil drops out of the class.
explanation.walkthrough: In RAIL the A, 'with ace dropping', moves down one place to give RIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial is a teaching session for a small group, a kind of class.

clue.text: Outstanding victory, own goal's let in

indicators.note: let in says the victory goes inside the own goal

parts.note: OG is the football abbreviation for an own goal
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A remarkable win that conceded an own goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt still outstanding is owing, unpaid and due.

clue.text: One on horse, on one's high horse?

definitions.meaning: a horseman, especially a Royalist trooper of the Civil War
being haughty and disdainful, a sense of the adjective

explanation.definitionFit: A cavalier was a mounted soldier, and as an adjective the word means arrogantly offhand.

clue.text: Cuddle nice soft lassie, all losing heart

indicators.note: all losing heart says each of the three words drops its middle, leaving its outside letters

explanation.surface: Hugging a nice, gentle girl, all of them heartbroken.
explanation.definitionFit: To nestle is to snuggle up close, the same as cuddling.

clue.text: Head with turn in exam whipping boy

indicators.note: in says the head and turn sit inside the exam

parts.note: SAT is a standard school exam
a cape or headland is a head of land jutting into the sea
a turn in a game is a go

explanation.surface: A schoolboy turns his head in an exam and gets beaten for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A whipping boy took punishment for a prince's misdeeds, so the phrase now means anyone blamed for others' faults.

clue.text: Degenerate follows this compiler's appearance

indicators.note: follows puts the word for degenerate after the setter's I'M

parts.note: the setter speaking of themself: this compiler is = I am, shortened to I'M
to age is to decline or degenerate

explanation.surface: The setter remarks that something decayed comes after their own looks.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is the outward look or likeness of someone, their appearance.

clue.text: Perform Shylock for one changing sides to begin

indicators.note: the first letter, L for left, swaps to the other side, R for right

parts.note: Shylock, the moneylender in The Merchant of Venice, is an example of a lender

explanation.surface: An actor performs Shylock, switching sides at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To render a song or part is to perform or deliver it.

clue.text: Show-off's end of short cloth dress reflected

indicators.note: reflected says the whole string is read as in a mirror, backwards
end of picks the final letter of the word short

parts.note: a rag is a piece of cloth
garb is clothing or dress

explanation.surface: A show-off's skimpy cloth dress is seen in the mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Show-off's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay. 'reflected' reverses TRAGGARB.
explanation.definitionFit: A boastful person who shows off is a braggart, a synonym.

clue.text: Man weakened after being distressed?

parts.note: distressed is read as de-tressed, having the locks of hair cut off, the source of the biblical strongman's loss of strength

explanation.surface: A man left weak after being upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'distressed' as 'de-tressed': Delilah had his hair cut, and with it went his strength.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical strongman of Judges lost his might when Delilah had his hair shorn.

clue.text: Woman is accommodating, holding up shoe

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the letters are read from bottom to top
holding says the words woman is accommodating contain the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A woman makes room for someone by holding up a shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Woman is accommodating' backwards: the letters NISACCOM, read upwards, give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A moccasin is a soft leather slip-on shoe of Native American origin.

clue.text: Idiot, before engagement, getting quietly taken for stone

indicators.note: taken says the quiet letter is taken into the combined idiot and engagement
before puts the idiot ahead of the engagement

parts.note: a sap is a fool
a hire is an engagement of someone's services
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A fool, just before getting engaged, is quietly fobbed off with a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapphire is a precious blue gemstone, an example of a stone.

clue.text: Notice surprised expression over Queen seeing bottom

parts.note: a poster is a public notice

indicators.note: over says the cry is turned over, reading backwards

parts.note: oi is a startled cry to get someone's attention
R is regina, queen, as in royal cyphers

explanation.surface: Someone sees a notice above the Queen and cries out in surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Posterior is a jocular word for the buttocks, a person's bottom.

clue.text: President takes one in with his empty achievements

indicators.note: takes says the president takes something into him
in says the one goes inside the president

parts.note: Donald Trump was the US president when the puzzle appeared
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: empty says the word his loses its middle, leaving its outside letters

explanation.surface: The president boasts of his hollow accomplishments.
explanation.definitionFit: Triumphs are great successes or victories, i.e. achievements.

clue.text: 'Science' of garden feature incorporating water centrally

indicators.note: incorporating says the garden feature takes another letter into it

parts.note: a rockery is a garden bed of stones and plants

indicators.note: centrally picks the middle letter of the word water

explanation.surface: Building a rock garden with water running through it is called a science.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes round 'Science' hint that the study of rockets is only loosely a science.
explanation.definitionFit: The study and building of rockets is a branch of engineering, which the quotes playfully call a science.

clue.text: Vegetable, practically uncooked food

indicators.note: practically says the word is not quite whole, losing its last letter

parts.note: raw means uncooked
a dish is a prepared food

explanation.surface: A vegetable eaten almost raw as food.
explanation.definitionFit: A radish is a crisp red root vegetable often eaten raw.

clue.text: Recall large talent and sex appeal of stars

indicators.note: recall is read as call back, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
art is skill or talent

explanation.surface: Remembering the big talent and allure of film stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Astral is the adjective for things relating to the stars.

clue.text: Way to keep air rising inside dish

indicators.note: to keep says the way holds another piece within it

parts.note: a lane is a way or road

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, says the letters read upwards

parts.note: gas is air, as in vapour

explanation.surface: A way of keeping the air rising in a cooked dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' only reinforces the containment signalled by 'to keep'; 'dish' looks like part of the surface but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is a baked Italian dish of pasta sheets layered with sauce.

clue.text: Debate of European Union progress set back

indicators.note: set back is read as put backwards, turning the whole string round

parts.note: to go is to progress
laid means set down

explanation.surface: An argument about the EU's progress being held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses EUGOLAID; 'set' does double duty as both the last piece and part of the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialogue is a discussion or exchange of views, so a debate.

clue.text: Beat United in no-score draw?

indicators.note: in says the team name goes inside the draw

parts.note: a nil-nil draw is written as two noughts
Utd is the usual football abbreviation for United

explanation.surface: Could United win in a goalless draw?
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to surpass or defeat them, to beat them.

clue.text: Iron, occasionally nicked, sold firstly to them?

definitions.text: Iron, occasionally nicked, sold firstly to them?

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: occasionally picks every other letter of the word nicked
firstly picks the opening letter of the word sold

explanation.surface: Stolen iron gets sold on to receivers.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: nicked (stolen) iron is sold to receivers of stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang a fence is someone who buys and resells stolen goods.

clue.text: Periodically call in mob to top

indicators.note: periodically picks letters at regular intervals, every other one, from the words that follow

explanation.surface: Calling in the crowd from time to time to reach the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb is to go up to the top, ascending.

clue.text: Reportedly pitched forward

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is as heard, a sound-alike

parts.note: in cricket a bowled ball is pitched, delivered to the batsman

explanation.surface: A cricket ball was said to be pitched forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Bold can mean impudent or presumptuous, so forward.

clue.text: Speedy with incredibly fast time initially

definitions.text: Speedy with incredibly fast time initially

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: Something quick, with a remarkably fast time from the off.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials of the first five words spell the answer, and the whole clue describes it too.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift means fast-moving, a direct synonym of speedy.

clue.text: Showing potential power, tick over in revolution

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

indicators.note: in puts the reversed tick inside the revolution

parts.note: a rising is an uprising or revolution

indicators.note: over says the word for tick is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a mo (moment) is a tick, as in 'just a tick'

explanation.surface: An engine's power ticking over as it revolves.
explanation.definitionFit: Something promising shows signs of future success, so it shows potential.

clue.text: Great, some inverted navel bared is no crime

indicators.note: inverted says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Showing off a bare belly button is no great offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Considerable means large in size or amount, so great.
